title: Logs, health and metrics
request: Running the product in containers leaves operators blind. Add structured JSON logs with a request id (never a secret, a prompt or a data value), a liveness route and a readiness route (database and file storage reachable), counters for requests, job durations, failures and model usage in Prometheus format on a port that is not public, and show job failures on the Compute page.
spec: JSON log lines with a request id, the route pattern, status, time and the person's and workspace's ids; GET /healthz (process up) and GET /readyz (database and file storage reachable, 503 naming what failed); Prometheus counters on DCLAB_METRICS_PORT for requests, jobs, failures and model requests, tokens and euros; failed or interrupted jobs listed on the Compute page with Retry.
plan: Check what is installed for metrics and how the server logs today; write a small metrics registry in Prometheus text format rather than add a dependency.

Write dclab_rnd/observe.py (JSON formatter, request id, metrics registry and its own HTTP server), the request middleware, /healthz and /readyz (public in the accounts guard), job counters in the worker, model counters in the gateway, and a Failures panel on the Compute page.
Set DCLAB_LOG_FORMAT=json and the metrics ports in the containers, use /readyz as the compose health check, document the settings.
Write tests/test_observe.py; run make check-all and the reviewer; fix the seven findings with a test each; gate again and commit, keeping the 12.5 work started meanwhile out of this commit.

decisions.decision: Log and label the route's pattern, never the path.
decisions.why: Paths hold project and draft ids, and query strings and bodies can hold data; the pattern keeps the label set bounded and free of values.

decisions.decision: Metrics on a port of their own that the containers never publish, off unless DCLAB_METRICS_PORT is set.
decisions.why: Counters by route and workspace are operational detail that must not be public, and a local run needs no extra port.

decisions.decision: A metrics port that cannot be bound turns metrics off with a warning instead of stopping the process.
decisions.why: Observability must never be the reason the product does not start.

decisions.decision: Readiness runs at most one probe at a time and gives up after 5 seconds.
decisions.why: A database that drops packets would otherwise block one thread per probe until the TCP timeout and starve the executor the request guard also uses.

change: New dclab_rnd/observe.py; a request middleware in the server (request id kept from a proxy when it is a plain token, one JSON line per request, counters); /healthz and /readyz in routers/core.py and public in the accounts guard; job counters and a 'job ended' log line in jobs/worker.py; model request, token and euro counters in the gateway; a failures() list on the Compute page with Retry; docker-compose and the Dockerfile set the log format and metrics ports; .env.example documents them.

findings.defect: Metric labels could grow without bound through the HTTP method.
findings.scenario: The image runs uvicorn on h11, which accepts any token as a method; 50 requests with random methods such as XABC12 added 150 new series, each answered 403, with no sign-in needed, so anyone could grow the process's memory and Prometheus's series.
findings.cause: request.method was used as a label as sent.
findings.fix: Map the method to a fixed set (GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS) or OTHER, in the counters and the log line.
findings.test: A test in tests/test_observe.py for this finding (the commit says each of the seven is fixed and tested).

findings.defect: A busy or invalid metrics port stopped the app or the worker from starting.
findings.scenario: A developer sets DCLAB_METRICS_PORT=9464 in .env as .env.example suggests; the server and a separate worker both load it and collide, and the worker dies with 'Address already in use'; every parallel test process also loads .env and runs a lifespan, so every test file after the first fails to start its app. DCLAB_METRICS_PORT=abc raised a raw ValueError.
findings.cause: The bind and the int() ran unguarded in the lifespan and in the worker's main.
findings.fix: Wrap the bind in try/except OSError and log that metrics are off; check the value as an integer port in problems().
findings.test: A test in tests/test_observe.py for this finding (the commit says each of the seven is fixed and tested).

findings.defect: Counters lost precision after six digits.
findings.scenario: A token counter at 123456789 rendered as 1.23457e+08; token counts reach millions within days and probe counts within weeks, after which rate() and increase() move in steps of 10, 100, 1000.
findings.fix: Render with full precision (repr of the float).
findings.test: A test in tests/test_observe.py for this finding (the commit says each of the seven is fixed and tested).

findings.defect: A 500 response carried no request id.
findings.scenario: A route raising ValueError, called with X-Request-ID: trace-err-0001, returned 500 without the header: the error middleware outside this middleware built the response. Errors are when a person most needs an id to quote.
findings.cause: call_next re-raised and the response was built outside the middleware.
findings.fix: Catch the exception in the middleware, log the line and return a JSON 500 with the request id in the body and the header.
findings.test: A test in tests/test_observe.py for this finding (the commit says each of the seven is fixed and tested).

findings.defect: A dead worker's jobs were never counted as failures.
findings.scenario: The worker container is killed for memory while running a stage; another process's recover() marks the job interrupted, but dclab_jobs_total and dclab_job_failures_total do not move and nothing is logged, though this is the failure an alert most needs.
findings.cause: Only execute() counted; the recovery path did not.
findings.fix: recover() counts the job as interrupted with its time and writes the 'job ended' line.
findings.test: A test in tests/test_observe.py for this finding (the commit says each of the seven is fixed and tested).

findings.defect: A 429's log line had no person or workspace.
findings.scenario: Someone hits the rate limit: the line says user null, workspace null, so an operator cannot see who hit it.
findings.cause: request.state.who was set after the rate-limit check returned.
findings.fix: Set it right after the person is identified.
findings.test: A test in tests/test_observe.py for this finding (the commit says each of the seven is fixed and tested).

findings.defect: Plain-text mode printed an empty line per request.
findings.scenario: Without DCLAB_LOG_FORMAT=json (the default for make notebook, make dev and make test) every request, including the Compute page's 2.5-second poll, printed a bare 'INFO dclab request' with no route, status or id, flooding the output the parallel runner prints for a failing file.
findings.cause: The plain formatter dropped the record's fields.
findings.fix: Plain text logs only server errors, with the same fields.
findings.test: A test in tests/test_observe.py for this finding (the commit says each of the seven is fixed and tested).

outcome: Done (412525c): one JSON line per request and per job that ends badly, a request id on every response including a 500, /healthz and /readyz used by the compose health check, Prometheus counters on a private port, and failures with Retry on the Compute page. Seven review findings fixed and tested. Open: each process serves its own counters and they reset on restart; a load balancer probing by IP needs that name allowed; a streamed answer's time is the time to its first byte; uvicorn's error lines and a job's traceback stay plain text.
lessons: Every metric label must come from a closed set; anything the client sends, even the HTTP method, can explode the series.
Observability must fail soft: a busy metrics port should turn metrics off, never stop the server.
Test the error path of a request-id feature first: a 500 is where the id matters most and where middleware order loses it.
